S1.headline: Children are not small adults.
S1.body: The panel's own sentence says children go through continuous physiologic and anatomic changes, which is why a model fitted to adults is not the model a child needs.

S2.headline: The panel named where the gap is.

document.body: Artificial intelligence (AI) applications have transformed radiology, yet pediatric medical imaging remains substantially underrepresented in AI development, validation, regulation, and implementation.

S2.cite: c1 c2 c3 c4   TEXAS AI DOCKET

S3.headline: Off label, in the panel's own words.
S3.body: The review names the practice among its ethical and regulatory concerns for children, beside consent for secondary data use and the need for postdeployment surveillance.

S4.headline: They sealed the model before they tested it.
S4.body: The second paper fitted its model on one brain metastasis cohort, kept 7 features, and then ran the fixed model on 69 patients it had never met.
S4.cite: c16 c17 c20 c22 c26   TEXAS AI DOCKET

S5.headline: Fitted to 198. Tested on 69.
S5.body: The model was built on a public cohort. It then ran on an independent cohort without refitting.
labels: 198 THE COHORT IT WAS BUILT ON
69 THE COHORT IT HAD NOT MET

S6.headline: It did worse on the patients it had never seen.
S6.body: It scored 0.615 on the brain metastasis cohort it was built on and 0.574 on the cohort it had not met. The paper's own intervals are 0.543 to 0.687 and 0.491 to 0.658, and its authors ask for cautious use.
S6.cite: c16 c22 c24 c25   TEXAS AI DOCKET

S7.kicker2: What the record does not hold
S7.headline: Neither record puts a figure on this.
S7.body: The review's record names insufficient external validation and carries no measurement of how far outside the training data a child sits.

S8.headline: Two of the panel's departments are Texan.
S8.body: The two here are at Baylor College of Medicine with Texas Children's Hospital in Houston, and at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas. The three leaving the sheet are the children's hospitals of Boston, Cincinnati and Philadelphia.
S8.cite: c11 c12 c13 c14 c15   TEXAS AI DOCKET

S9.headline: Ask what it was validated on.
S9.body: A parent can ask at the desk what population each imaging tool was validated on. The Food and Drug Administration's device list carries the word pediatric in two device names and nowhere in its own text. The panel wants pediatric infrastructure, not adult tools reused.
S9.cite: c7 c10 c27   TEXAS AI DOCKET
